title: Skills portfolio
intro: The BUT Informatique is built around six competency blocks from the French national framework. For each, I set out the level targeted in the final year, the evidence drawn from my work and projects, the progression between the S4 internship and the S6 apprenticeship, and a short reflective note.
todoNote: Level titles and critical learning outcomes are to be aligned with the exact wording of the AGED framework (marked "to be confirmed").

realiser.niveauLibelle: Adapt applications across a range of platforms and business needs (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Evolve an application to make it safer, more reliable and easier to maintain (to be confirmed)
Design and implement an application's tests (to be confirmed)
Develop complex software applications (to be confirmed)
realiser.description: On the apprenticeship, "developing" mostly meant building decision-support indicators and well-tooled Python applications. I carried projects from requirements through to deployment, with an emphasis on maintainability: externalised configuration, tests, documentation, packaging.
realiser.preuves: The DESCAR-T decision-support platform (DAX indicators, semantic model) and above all QC Report Builder — a desktop application in MVC architecture, tested with pytest, distributed as a Python package and a standalone executable. Outside the apprenticeship, Didactypo and Self Tracker cover full-stack web development.
realiser.progression: In S4 I built dashboards from specifications. In S6 I design the application architecture and own the full lifecycle, tests and maintenance documentation included.
realiser.noteReflexive: I've learned that "developing" doesn't stop at code that works: the value of an internal tool is in whether someone else can pick it up. That's what made me systematise external configuration and technical documentation.
axesProgression: Peer code review, absent on my role

optimiser.niveauLibelle: Analyse and optimise applications against measurable criteria (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Analyse a problem methodically: break it down, measure, compare (to be confirmed)
Compare algorithmic solutions and pick the one best suited to the context and constraints (to be confirmed)
Assess the impact of a change on performance and reliability (to be confirmed)
optimiser.description: Optimisation in my work was less about the speed of an algorithm than the efficiency of a process: replacing weekly Excel manipulation with a model that refreshes itself, or a one-hour manual quality check with automatic generation. The choice of star-schema modelling is itself an optimisation decision, driven by the shape of the queries.
optimiser.preuves: The Python quality-control tools, which automate repetitive manual work; the decision-support platform, whose model was designed for query performance and definition harmonisation; on the AI POC, the choice of models that can run locally under a response-time constraint. Outside the apprenticeship, the graph algorithms in Secured Air Enforcer.
optimiser.progression: In S4 I optimised the rendering of existing dashboards. In S6 I made architecture decisions (star schema, indicator granularity) and model choices, arguing the trade-offs.
optimiser.noteReflexive: My optimisation instinct is still stronger on processes than on code itself. The AI POC showed me how hard a system's robustness and response time are to hold, and that's an area I want to go deeper on.
axesProgression: Choosing and tuning machine-learning and LLM models

administrer.niveauLibelle: Deploy and secure services within an information system (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Design and deploy a service in a constrained environment (to be confirmed)
Secure services and data: permissions, partitioning, compliance (to be confirmed)
Install and configure a workstation and its runtime environment (to be confirmed)
administrer.description: My relationship with system administration came through deploying and distributing tools — publishing to Power BI Cloud, packaging standalone executables, setting up a local environment for running language models — and through treating data partitioning as a native constraint of the model, not a layer bolted on at reporting time.
administrer.preuves: Distributing QC Report Builder (package and executable for machines without a development environment), the local infrastructure of the AI POC, and the security framing of the decision-support platform with the CIO and the DPO: export frequency, anonymisation, storage. Outside the apprenticeship, my homelab (Docker, Traefik, self-hosted services, monitoring).
administrer.progression: In S4 deployment wasn't my concern. In S6 I handled publishing, distribution and local execution of my deliverables, and took part in security and GDPR-compliance decisions.
administrer.noteReflexive: This is the block where my experience is most fragmented: plenty of deployment and application security, less system administration proper. My homelab is my best learning ground on that front.
axesProgression: Containerisation and orchestration: advanced Docker, Kubernetes

gerer-donnees.niveauLibelle: Design and implement a decision-support information system while guaranteeing data quality and security (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Design a data model suited to a use case: transactional, decision-support, longitudinal (to be confirmed)
Implement an extract, transform and load chain (to be confirmed)
Guarantee the quality, traceability and confidentiality of data (to be confirmed)
Exploit data for decision-making (to be confirmed)
gerer-donnees.description: This is the heart of my apprenticeship and of the AGED track. I worked on a real-world national clinical registry: an evolving schema (around thirty case-report-form versions), a conditional schema (variables that only apply to certain patient subsets), a longitudinal structure (each item collected around twenty times per patient), strict partitioning between partners. Designing a decision-support model on that basis means handling granularity and the meaning of missing values explicitly.
gerer-donnees.preuves: The DESCAR-T decision-support platform: star-schema semantic model, SAS and Power Query chain, indicator verification against the reference extractions, work under MR-004. The AI POC, with an ETL into a dedicated SQLite database and SQL generation. Outside the apprenticeship, the breast cancer dataset and the Fou2Food database.
gerer-donnees.progression: In S4 I extracted and cleaned data with SAS and SQL against a defined plan. In S6 I design the data model, weigh up indicator granularity and own the quality and confidentiality approach end to end.
gerer-donnees.noteReflexive: This registry taught me that the difficulty of a data project is almost never volume: it's structure, history and veracity. Distinguishing "not recorded", "not applicable to this pathology" and "not applicable to this form version" before any aggregation has become a reflex.

conduire.niveauLibelle: Take part in designing and implementing an information-system project (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Analyse a need and assess its feasibility (to be confirmed)
Run an iterative approach with regular deliveries (to be confirmed)
Prioritise and make trade-offs based on value and constraints (to be confirmed)
Ensure a project's tracking, documentation and closure (to be confirmed)
conduire.description: I led three projects in parallel, on different timelines, with no dedicated project manager on my scope. My method was consistent: requirements workshops, a validated mockup or functional version, a deliberately early production release, then weekly iteration on usage feedback, and closure with documentation and training.
conduire.preuves: The decision-support platform (workshops with four project managers, a validated mockup, iteration over several months, a regulatory framing meeting), the Python tools (the same approach repeated four times), and the AI POC — framed as exploratory and stopped with an owned conclusion when the organisation's priorities changed. Outside the apprenticeship, Didactypo, where I was scrum master.
conduire.progression: In S4 I contributed to a project framed by others. In S6 I frame the need, plan, prioritise between competing projects and own the decision to pause a project.
conduire.noteReflexive: I've learned that an early, imperfect delivery, owned as such, beats a perfect deliverable shipped too late: it turns the user into a source of feedback rather than just a recipient. Accepting the AI POC being stopped was also a lesson: a project can be a success without going to production, if its conclusion is clear.
axesProgression: Estimation and planning on long projects

equipe.niveauLibelle: Integrate into, contribute to and help evolve the practices of an IT team (to be confirmed)
apprentissagesCritiques: Adapt communication to stakeholders from different fields and technical levels (to be confirmed)
Share knowledge and support others' upskilling (to be confirmed)
Contribute to evolving the team's tools and practices (to be confirmed)
Carry out and share technology watch (to be confirmed)
equipe.description: As the only person in my role, I mostly "worked in a team" cross-functionally: with data managers, SAS programmers, biostatisticians, project managers, a project lead, a doctor, the CIO and the DPO. Moving from a biostatistician audience to a project-manager audience on the same data was the most formative communication exercise. I also helped evolve the team's practices.
equipe.preuves: The decision-support platform, with two distinct audiences and a presentation at a scientific café; supporting the rollout of Visual Studio Code and Git, the training and best-practice guides; contributing to the IT team's new BI documentation standard by documenting my own indicators to it first; internal talks and webinars on AI, standardisation and automation. Outside the apprenticeship, the scrum-master role on Didactypo.
equipe.progression: In S4 I integrated into a team and reported back. In S6 I trained colleagues, spread practices and contributed to team standards.
equipe.noteReflexive: Having no peer on my role forced me to make my choices understandable and assessable by people who aren't specialists in my tools. That constraint made teaching a core skill, one I also draw on in my volunteering.
axesProgression: Working in a developer team with established rituals
